candidates.headline: Regional worker housing opens its doors
candidates.summary:
Local tradespeople and 11 businesses helped deliver the cabins, which were built using modular construction for faster installation.

In Lorne, where hospitality businesses rely on seasonal staff, eight new units can house up to 32 Lorne Hotel workers. This will help the hotel secure staff while freeing up other local accommodation. Geelong Building Company built the units, supporting dozens of regional construction workers.

In Warrnambool, construction is underway to deliver cabins at Shipwreck Bay Holiday Park to provide 32 bedrooms for local workers, including those in health and education. The park’s location near public transport, parkland and the town centre will also help workers and their families settle into the community.

These investments are all made possible by our Regional Worker Accommodation Fund, which is helping employers fill jobs, keep essential services running and support regional growth.

candidates.headline: Unlocking land for business investment near Seymour
candidates.summary:
We’ve invested in early works to establish a new industrial precinct near Seymour – paving the way for job growth and business investment in one of Victoria’s fastest growing municipalities.

This includes a new intersection at the Hilldene Employment Precinct, part of a more than $1.6 million investment by the Victorian Government.

Construction of the Seymour-Tooborac Road intersection will begin in coming weeks, marking the final stage of early works at the site and opening the precinct to businesses looking to establish or expand in central Victoria.

This investment will help Mitchell Shire Council unlock the precinct to address industrial land shortages and has also supported a masterplan for the site, engineering designs and environmental works to rezone the 50-hectare precinct for industrial use.

candidates.headline: Aussie staple arrives at Gippsland manufacturing precinct
candidates.summary:
The 200-year-old company is building its new Morwell Parcel Facility, which is set to bring jobs and an economic boost to the Latrobe Valley.

The 69-hectare Gippsland Logistics and Manufacturing Precinct promises to become the centre of industrial growth for the region. It has received support from all three levels of government to install essential infrastructure – including $14 million from the Victorian Government.

This infrastructure - including power, water, sewerage, electricity and NBN connections - is attracting private investment and further development, with Australia Post’s new facility leading the way.

Once fully developed, the industrial precinct will deliver a major employment boost for the region. More than 70 jobs are being created through the staged delivery of essential infrastructure, and up to 900 additional jobs are expected once the land is fully tenanted.

candidates.summary:
The City of Greater Bendigo has completed a major project to improve the Bendigo Library’s public toilet and parent facilities to comply with the current National Construction Code and make them safer and easier to access.

Today Member for Bendigo West Maree Edwards, Goldfields Library CEO Mark Hands and City of Greater Bendigo Healthy Communities and Environments Director Jess Howard inspected the new facilities.

“The new facilities have transformed the library and the City is very appreciative of the funding received from the Victorian Government’s Living Libraries Infrastructure Program to undertake this project.”

The project was funded by a $412,586 grant from the Victorian Government’s Living Libraries Infrastructure Program and the City of Greater Bendigo.

candidates.headline: $2M boost to unlock next stage of GV Link Enterprise Park - The Shepparton Adviser
candidates.summary: GREATER Shepparton’s push to attract new businesses and jobs has received a $2 million boost, with the Victorian Government funding set to help progress the next stage of GV Link Enterprise Park. Greater Shepparton City Council welcomed the investment, which will fund critical infrastructure needed to prepare additional industrial lots for development and attract future business investment. Mayor Geoff Akers said the funding was a major vote of confidence in the region’s economic future, with demand for industrial land continuing to grow. Council will now progress detailed design work for Stage 2 and seek expressions of interest for the remaining lots to better understand industry demand. The expansion is expected to create opportunities for business growth, freight and logistics investment, and employment across Shepparton and the wider Goulburn Valley.

candidates.headline: A funding story - The Shepparton Adviser
candidates.summary:
The Fairley Leadership Program began in 1997 with modest funding and a belief that investing in local people could strengthen an entire region.

Government investment continued between 2020 and 2023 through the Regional Community Leadership Program Fund and Department of Jobs, Precincts and Regions.

Throughout its history, that investment has been complemented by participant scholarships, including support from organisations such as the Gardiner Foundation and Hugh Williamson Foundation.

Their contribution also demonstrates that sustaining regional leadership is not the responsibility of any one organisation or sector. It is something businesses, governments, philanthropic organisations and communities can collectively invest in, helping ensure the next generation of local leaders has the same opportunity to step forward.

candidates.headline: BFNL returns to self-administration; more changes to women’s football
candidates.summary:
The BFNL has moved to a new self-administration model, effective from earlier this week. Photo: Fort Bend Film Club.

A new self-management model will see the Bendigo Football Netball League (BFNL) assume direct responsibility for its governance, employment, administration, and operations.

The move to self-administration – effective from last Monday (2 November) – is one of several changes to future football administration arrangements, announced by AFL Central Victoria, as part of its Regional Administration Centres (RAC) Transition Project.

AFL Central Victoria regional manager Cameron Tomlins said the project was designed to support the evolution of football administration by strengthening league capability, governance, and long-term sustainability while ensuring competitions continue to operate with minimal disruption for clubs, players, volunteers, umpires and communities.
